title: Maintaining Proper Pipe Pitch for Waste Flow
description: Drain lines require a balanced slope to transport both liquids and solids effectively. If a drainage pipe has insufficient pitch, water slows down and allows heavy debris or suspended solids to settle at the bottom, eventually causing recurring clogs. Conversely, excessive slope causes liquids to rush ahead, leaving solid waste behind to accumulate along dry pipe walls. Proper maintenance involves routinely verifying pipe hangers and supports, especially in exposed basement runs or crawlspaces, to prevent sags and belly formation over time. Maintaining correct alignment according to applicable plumbing codes prevents chronic blockages.
